body.statement:
In the pure structure-agnostic class \(\mathcal P(\varepsilon_n,\delta_n)\) of BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, defined for two arbitrary nuisance estimates whose \(L^2\) errors are at most \(\varepsilon_n\) and \(\delta_n\), Section 2 states for its single mean functional \(\psi\) that no estimator has convergence rate faster than
\[
n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n.
\]
The source says that analogous results apply armwise to the control mean, so the display supplies an analogous one-arm lower-bound template there.  It does not by itself establish a joint two-arm full-ATE minimax equivalence, a two-product lower bound for one common ATE experiment, or a matching upper bound for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

source.verbatim_statement: Given two arbitrary estimators $\widehat\omega(x)$ and $\widehat\mu(x)$, the class $\mathcal{P}(\epsilon_n,\delta_n)$ consists of all densities such that $\lVert\widehat\omega-\omega\rVert\leq\epsilon_n$ and $\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert\leq\delta_n$. Our first result is that the rate of convergence of any estimator of $\psi$ over this class cannot be faster than $n^{-1/2}+\epsilon_n\cdot\delta_n$.

attestation.note: Verified against the authors’ arXiv:2405.08525 source archive (version dated 2024-12-13), main_v2.tex, Section 2 (Structure-agnostic viewpoint), opening of the purely structure-agnostic subsection. Section 1 defines psi as the treated potential-outcome mean and explicitly says the same results apply to the control mean; applying the armwise statement to their difference gives the stated full-ATE sum up to constants. The same paper’s Section 1 AIPW decomposition supplies the matching upper product rate under bounded inverse propensity.

body.justification: This cited leaf records the source paper's lower-rate statement for one mean functional in its pure structure-agnostic class.
body.gap: The source supports an analogous armwise template, but the cited passage does not prove a joint two-arm ATE minimax equivalence or matching upper bound for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).
body.consumer: It supplies only an armwise lower-bound algebraic form for the sanity comparison in the regular-benchmark proposition.
